panels.title: Rollouts completed / min (by outcome)
panels.description: gym_rollout_completed_total — throughput and success rate. Are evals progressing?

panels.title: Rollout duration (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: gym_rollout_duration_ms — end-to-end time per rollout.

panels.title: Model call duration (p50 / p95 / p99, by dialect)
panels.description: gym_model_call_duration_ms — total model-call latency, grouped by service_name (the emitting process) and dialect rather than nemo_gym_server_name, which resource_to_telemetry_conversion overwrites on this metric.

panels.title: Model time-to-first-byte (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: gym_model_time_to_first_byte_ms — streaming TTFB, separate from total call duration.

panels.title: Sandbox startup duration (p50 / p95 / p99, by provider)
panels.description: gym_sandbox_startup_duration_ms — only covers sandboxes created via nemo_gym.sandbox.api.AsyncSandbox (e.g. the swebench resources server's verification sandbox). Harnesses that drive their own container lifecycle outside AsyncSandbox (e.g. mini_swe_agent_2's minisweagent-library sandbox) are not represented here.

panels.title: Verify duration (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: gym_verify_duration_ms — resources-server /verify latency.

panels.title: Concurrency queue-wait duration (p50 / p95 / p99, by site)
panels.description: gym_concurrency_queue_wait_duration_ms — time spent waiting to acquire a TimedSemaphore, per call site. Duration only, not a live queue-depth/active-slots gauge (see plan Phase 1 item 5).

panels.title: Verify success rate
panels.description: gym_verify_success_rate — cumulative fraction since process start, not a windowed rate.

panels.title: Process CPU % (by service)
panels.description: gym_process_cpu_percent — scoped to each Gym server's own Python PID only, not its child process tree (Enroot/OpenClaw/unsquashfs/sandbox processes are not included; see plan Phase 1 item 1).

panels.title: Host memory (used vs total)
panels.description: gym_host_memory_used_mib / gym_host_memory_total_mib — host-wide, not per-process.

panels.title: GPU utilization % (by GPU index)
panels.description: gym_process_gpu_utilization_percent — polled via nvidia-smi every gpu_sample_interval_s, filtered by CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES when parseable (falls back to reporting all GPUs otherwise). Every process on the host reports the same host-wide reading redundantly.

panels.title: GPU memory (used vs total, by GPU index)
HTTP retries (rate, by reason) / timeouts
panels.description: gym_http_retry_total / gym_http_timeout_total — ServerClient retry loop. Separate from gym_sandbox_create_retry_total (Daytona-specific sandbox-create retries), not plotted here.

panels.title: Active servers (fleet size)
panels.description: gym_servers_active — orchestrator-only gauge counting server *processes* in the fleet, not concurrent rollout workers.

panels.title: Sandbox exec duration (p50 / p95 / p99, by provider)
panels.description: gym_sandbox_exec_duration_ms — one command's wall-clock time inside an already-provisioned sandbox. Same AsyncSandbox-only coverage caveat as sandbox startup.

panels.title: Tool-call duration (p50 / p95 / p99, by tool name)
panels.description: gym_tool_call_duration_ms — requires telemetry.span_groups to include tool_call (part of per_rollout/all, not default). Only covers tool routes on a resources server, via ToolCallTelemetryMiddleware; skipped entirely for a server with expose_tools_over_mcp direct-dispatch (see nemo_gym/mcp_auto_exposure.py).

panels.title: Concurrency: limit / active / available / queued (by site)
panels.description: gym_concurrency_limit / .active / .available / .queue_depth — live state, not just after-the-fact wait duration. "Active == limit (available == 0) and queue_depth > 0" is a bottlenecked semaphore.

panels.title: Concurrency admission cancelled (rate, by site)
panels.description: gym_concurrency_admission_cancelled_total — a caller's wait for a semaphore permit was cancelled before admission (e.g. its own timeout fired first). Gym's semaphores have no reject-on-full policy, so this is the one abnormal-admission signal that exists.

panels.title: Agent turn count per rollout (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: gym_agent_turn_count — recorded post-hoc at rollout completion from the assembled trajectory (Gym's agent harnesses have no live per-turn span). Requires telemetry.span_groups to include agent.

panels.title: Agent turn duration (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: gym_agent_turn_duration_ms — derived from the gap between consecutive trajectory turn timestamps, not a live span.

panels.title: Process CPU: own PID vs. full process tree (by service)
panels.description: gym_process_cpu_percent (this PID only) vs. gym_process_tree_cpu_percent (this PID + every child -- Enroot, OpenClaw, unsquashfs, sandbox-runtime processes). The gap between the two lines is "actual job workload" the Gym-PID-only number was missing.

panels.title: Process-tree memory (by service)
panels.description: gym_process_tree_memory_used_mib — this process's RSS plus every child process, the process-scoped counterpart to the host-wide memory panel above.

panels.title: Tool-call CPU % / memory (p95, by tool name)
panels.description: gym_tool_call_cpu_percent / gym_tool_call_memory_used_mib — process-tree CPU/RSS sampled at each tool call's span close. An approximation ("how busy was the process during this call"), not an isolated per-call measurement — Gym cannot attribute CPU to one concurrent tool call in a multi-tenant process.

panels.title: % of rollout time spent in tool calls
panels.description: Derived, not a separate instrument: sum(tool-call time) / sum(rollout time) over the same window. Fleet-wide ratio across all rollouts in the window, not a per-rollout figure — a per-rollout breakdown needs the trace-level join the Pareto/efficiency script does (see nemo_gym/pareto_analysis.py), since OTel metrics deliberately do not carry rollout_id as a label.
